title: Twin-photon generation in a silicon nitride microresonator
authors: Franz Pacher, Haochen Yan, Alekhya Ghosh, Arghadeep Pal, Toby Bi, Hao Zhang, Lixing You, Hao Li, Daniela Salvoni, Shuangyou Zhang, Pascal Del'Haye
abstract: Photonic chips with silicon nitride ($\mathrm{Si_3N_4}$) microring resonators are well established as heralded single-photon sources, but their operation as frequency-degenerate twin-photon sources has not previously been demonstrated. Here, we realise a twin-photon source at telecommunication wavelengths in a $\mathrm{Si_3N_4}$ ring microresonator via an inverse four-wave mixing (FWM) process, in which two photons from spectrally distinct pumps are converted into a pair of identical twin photons. The measurements show a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio (CAR) of $5.4\pm0.6$. In addition, the microresonator functions as a heralded single-photon source through pump-degenerate spontaneous four-wave mixing (SFWM), exhibiting a spectral purity of $P=0.67\pm0.05$ and a heralded anti-bunching of $g^{(2)}_h(0)=0.0042\pm0.0015$. Together, these results demonstrate both photon-generation schemes on a single integrated $\mathrm{Si_3N_4}$ platform, highlighting its potential for scalable, tailored quantum light generation.
summary: The authors report the first demonstration of frequency-degenerate twin-photon generation and heralded single-photon emission using a single integrated silicon nitride microresonator. By measuring correlation functions like the CAR and $g^{(2)}_h(0)$, they prove the platform's capability to generate tailored quantum light sources on a scalable chip.
main_problem: The paper aims to demonstrate frequency-degenerate twin-photon generation and characterize a heralded single-photon source using a single integrated silicon nitride platform.
main_result: They successfully demonstrated both twin-photon generation (CAR up to 5.4) and heralded single-photon emission ($g^{(2)}_h(0) = 0.0042$) on the same chip.
method: The experiments utilized time-correlated single-photon counting with SNSPDs to measure second-order correlation functions ($g^{(2)}$) for both coincidence and heralded measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is a silicon nitride (Si3N4) microring resonator integrated on a photonic chip. Quantum light generation occurs via Four-Wave Mixing (FWM) processes (both non-degenerate for twins and degenerate for single photons).
key_observables: Coincidence-to-Accidental Ratio (CAR), heralded anti-bunching ($g^{(2)}_h(0)$), and spectral purity ($P$).
important_parameters: Telecom wavelengths, loaded quality factors ($Q \approx 10^5$), and pump powers up to $7 	ext{ dBm}$.
main_assumptions: The single-photon purity calculation assumes residual deviation is due to incomplete spectral isolation, and quantitative results are derived independently from coincidence counts rather than fitting procedures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic for inverse FWM (twin-photon source), the experimental setup using CDWDM, and plots showing $g^{(2)}$ cross-correlation vs. pump power, confirming the CAR dependence.
paper_structure: The paper details the realization of two distinct quantum light sources—twin-photon and single-photon—on one platform, characterized by measuring correlation functions ($g^{(2)}$) under different pumping conditions.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it demonstrates scalable, integrated quantum light sources (twin-photons and single photons) using established silicon photonics platforms, which is a core technology for quantum networking and computation.

(a) Schematic illustration of twin-photon generation through dual-pumped “inverse” four-wave mixing (FWM) in a ring mi- croresonator. (b) Cavity resonance spectrum showing the two pump modes (red and blue) positioned symmetrically about the central signal/idler mode (green), with a separation of one free spectral range (FSR) between each pump and the central mode. (c) Energy-level diagram: absorption of two photons with energies ℏω−1 and ℏω1 generates two degenerate photons with energies ℏω0, satisfying ω−1 + ω1 = 2ω0.

FIG. 3. Characterisation of the pump-degenerate SFWM-based heralded single-photon source. (a) g(2)-self-correlation measure- ment of the signal mode (Ch 33), with a fit to the data. The self-correlation exhibits a bunching peak with g(2)(0) = 1.67±0.05, corresponding to a Schmidt number of K = 1.49 ± 0.12 (≈1.5 effective modes). (b) Heralded g(2) h (τ) autocorrelation mea- surement, with a fit to the data, showing a pronounced anti-bunching dip with g(2) h (0) = 0.0042 ± 0.0015, well below the single-photon threshold. Error bars are calculated assuming Poissonian statistics of the recorded coincidence counts.
